trigger: a timed-out or output-capped ufw/iptables subprocess read whose exit_code still reads 0
classification_rationale: state| was derived from parsed subprocess output as soon as exit_code==0, without checking timed_out/output_truncated -- a partial read could parse as a confident, possibly wrong, enabled/disabled verdict
summary: ufw/iptables state| lacked the same completeness gate ruleset| already had (BR-01/02)

trigger: a signal delivered repeatedly during nft_dump's send()/poll() retry loops
classification_rationale: EINTR retry loops around send()/poll() were not bounded by the same steady_clock deadline as the rest of the dump logic; a signal storm could spin past the intended per-dump budget. Also fixed in the same round: a narrowing cast from a chrono::milliseconds count into struct timeval's tv_sec/tv_usec fields.
summary: EINTR retry loops unbounded by deadline; timeval narrowing cast

trigger: kernel DONE/ERROR payload's errno field equals exactly INT_MIN
classification_rationale: std::abs(INT_MIN) on a plain int is signed-overflow UB

trigger: operator reads the README/plugin-docs worked example expecting it to match live output
classification_rationale: schema/enum description is correct; only the illustrative captured transcript predates the new unconditional ruleset|<n> row -- doc-generation leg-hash gate structurally can't catch example staleness (hash covers column name/type only)
summary: stale Linux sample output transcript, missing ruleset|<n> row (convergent: docs-writer + cross-platform)

classification_rationale: comment attributed the !is_base_chain filtering guard to firewall_parsers.hpp; it actually lives in firewall_plugin.cpp's try_nftables_rules()
summary: misattributed file pointer in a comment

trigger: a regression in the composition of subprocess_complete()+nft_fallthrough_clamp specifically, not either half alone
classification_rationale: the security-guardian-HIGH completeness-gating fix (R1-SEC-1) was an inline ternary at each call site; only its two ingredients had direct test coverage, never the composed gate itself
summary: completeness-gating ternary itself untested (only subprocess_complete()/nft_fallthrough_clamp() independently tested)

trigger: socket()/bind() returns EPERM/EACCES (systemd RestrictAddressFamilies= omitting AF_NETLINK, or seccomp/AppArmor denying netlink)
classification_rationale: classify_open_errno's 'other' bucket (which EPERM/EACCES fell into) produced no diagnostic row at all -- silent fall-through indistinguishable from 'kernel genuinely has no NETLINK_NETFILTER'. Not false assurance (nothing claims a control holds); under-diagnosed absence.
summary: open_nft_socket EPERM/EACCES failures emitted no diagnostic token (converged with unhappy-path UP-1)

trigger: N/A -- cosmetic consistency only, not a leak (scope-exit RAII closes it either way)
classification_rationale: table_sock/chain_sock are both explicitly ->reset() after use; rule_sock was not, inconsistent with the stated fresh-fd-per-dump discipline
summary: rule_sock not explicitly reset for consistency with table_sock/chain_sock

trigger: the send() EINTR-retry loop's deadline elapses while still getting EINTR
classification_rationale: the deadline-elapsed-mid-EINTR-retry case fell through to the generic io_error default, rather than being reported as a timeout -- the abort itself was already correctly deadline-bounded, this was a diagnostic-label-only gap
summary: EINTR-deadline-elapsed case mislabeled as io_error instead of timeout

trigger: a reader of the assembled CHANGELOG.md scans .security.md-tier bullets specifically for security-relevant fixes
classification_rationale: the 3462 fragment (authored before the final commit) covers ruleset| completeness gating but not that state| itself is now also gated for ufw/iptables -- the actual security-guardian-HIGH fix. Converged independently with enterprise-readiness F1, whose stronger I7-raised-to-HIGH derivation governs the merged severity_mapped here.
summary: changelog fragment lagged the final HIGH fix; state| completeness gating undisclosed at security tier (converged with enterprise-readiness F1/F2)

trigger: an operator/auditor scanning .security.md fragments for security-relevant fixes in this release
classification_rationale: I7 raised to HIGH: the omission conceals a security-relevant behaviour change (a prior false-confident enabled/disabled report is now honestly gated) -- filing it only under .changed.md misrepresents severity to a changelog reader. Same underlying gap as R2-CA-1, this row's derivation governs (stronger of the two).
summary: no changelog fragment disclosed the ufw/iptables state| completeness fix at security tier

trigger: a customer relying on firewall state| readings sees an increase in unknown post-upgrade for hosts whose ufw/iptables reads were marginal
classification_rationale: I7 raised to HIGH: direct repo precedent exists for this exact plugin (the macOS firewall backend-key-change entry, the antivirus entry) -- both written because a per-device dashboard value changes shape/frequency on upgrade and would otherwise read as a regression. This PR causes the identical customer-visible effect with no upgrade note.
summary: no docs/user-manual/server-admin.md upgrade note for the state| completeness-gating behavior shift

trigger: a transient Windows COM enumeration failure (do_rules_windows) or a truncated/timed-out macOS pfctl read
classification_rationale: same failure class as R1-SEC-1 (a read that completed/partially-completed being reported as a confident, possibly wrong, verdict) but on Windows/macOS code this PR does not touch -- genuinely pre-existing, not introduced or newly-reachable by this diff. Derives HIGH by IMPACT (I3) alone, but PROVENANCE=pre-existing and the code is entirely outside this PR's Linux-only scope, so it does not gate this PR (Gate 7: a pre-existing finding outside accepted scope is filed, not fixed-in-place -- fixing it here would expand a Linux-scoped PR onto untouched platforms).
summary: Windows do_rules_windows COM-enumeration-failure and macOS pfctl reads lack the same completeness gating this PR adds for Linux

trigger: an nftables ruleset mutation lands between the chain-dump instant and the (up to several seconds later) rule-dump instant
classification_rationale: table/chain/rule dumps are 3 independent NLM_F_DUMP round-trips, not one transaction -- no cross-dump consistency check exists. Narrow race window, no corrupted-count path (each dump's own trusted gate still holds), so this stays SHOULD not a blocker.
summary: no cross-dump staleness signal across the 3 independent nftables dump round-trips

trigger: chain dump times out under its 1500ms sub-budget while the rule dump independently hits foreign_flood/oversized
classification_rationale: info.dump = chains_ok ? "rule" : "chain" always reports the chain failure reason when chain fails, silently dropping the rule dump's distinct failure info when both fail. Never a wrong state/ruleset value (trusted gate still blocks partial emission) -- diagnostic completeness only. Converged independently by unhappy-path and plugin-developer.
summary: simultaneous chain+rule dump failure reports only the chain's failure reason

trigger: persistent fd exhaustion (UP-4); sustained nftables churn from a competing tool (UP-5); a future ufw/iptables output-format drift (UP-6, speculative)
classification_rationale: three minor, independent NICE-severity items (double-emit guard, torn-token operational noise under churn, no output-shape backstop) -- none carry I1/I2/I3 impact so parking is available per Gate 7. Chaos-injector's own synthesis recommended these as backlog notes, not fault-injection scenarios.
summary: three minor NICE-severity diagnostic/UX gaps, parked together
